LanguageData.TunnelRaids.Settings.MechanoidTooltip: Mechanoid raids can burrow up from beneath the colony. Every such raid includes at least one tunneler mech, and its pawn budget is reduced like human tunnel raids. Requires the Biotech DLC. This is independent of the faction and xenotype selections below, which only affect humanlike raids.
LanguageData.TunnelRaids.Settings.MechanoidBiotechReq: Mechanoid tunnel raids require the Biotech DLC, which is not active. Your choice is kept for when it is.
LanguageData.TunnelRaids.Settings.BlockMuddyLabel: Block tunnel entrances on muddy terrain
LanguageData.TunnelRaids.Settings.BlockMuddyTooltip: Tunnel entrances will not open on mud, marshy soil, marsh or marsh flooding. The visible surface counts, so a floor built over mud is judged as that floor. Applies to humanlike and mechanoid tunnel raids. If no allowed spot exists, the raid arrives from the map edge instead. Raiders can still walk and fight on this terrain once they are out.
LanguageData.TunnelRaids.Settings.BlockRockyLabel: Block tunnel entrances on rocky terrain
LanguageData.TunnelRaids.Settings.BlockRockyTooltip: Tunnel entrances will not open on rough, rough-hewn or smoothed rock, volcanic rock, stone tile or flagstone floors. The visible surface counts, so a floor built over rock is judged as that floor. Applies to humanlike and mechanoid tunnel raids. If no allowed spot exists, the raid arrives from the map edge instead. Raiders can still walk and fight on this terrain once they are out.
LanguageData.TunnelRaids.Settings.FactionsHint: Only checked factions can use tunnels. Leave all unchecked to allow every eligible hostile humanlike faction. Mechanoid tunnel raids ignore this list.
LanguageData.TunnelRaids.Settings.XenotypesHint: This filter chooses factions that can naturally generate a selected xenotype. Tunnel raiders may also have other xenotypes.
LanguageData.TunnelRaids.Settings.XenotypesOverrideHi: All humanlike tunnel raiders will be generated with the single chosen xenotype, even if their faction would not naturally generate it.
LanguageData.TunnelRaids.Settings.BiotechRequired: Xenotype filters require the Biotech DLC, which is not active.
LanguageData.TunnelRaids.Settings.OverrideTooltip: Forces the selected xenotype on humanlike pawns generated for tunnel raids from any otherwise eligible humanlike faction. Other arrival modes are not affected.
LanguageData.TunnelRaids.Settings.OverrideDisabledToo: Select exactly one xenotype that can generate as a combatant to enable this option.
LanguageData.TunnelRaids.FactionIssue.PlayerFaction: This is a player faction and never raids.
LanguageData.TunnelRaids.FactionIssue.NotHumanlike: This faction is not humanlike, so it cannot use tunnels.
LanguageData.TunnelRaids.FactionIssue.RaidsForbidden: Raids from this faction are forbidden.
LanguageData.TunnelRaids.FactionIssue.NoCombatGroups: This faction has no combat pawn groups, so it cannot raid.
LanguageData.TunnelRaids.XenotypeIssue.NotCombatant: This xenotype cannot generate as a combatant, so it never appears in raids and cannot be used for the override.
LanguageData.TunnelRaids.Message.FactionNoNaturalMatc: {0} cannot naturally generate any selected xenotype, so it cannot use tunnels. Select a xenotype it can generate, uncheck {0}, or use the override.
LanguageData.TunnelRaids.Message.NoFactionMatchesXeno: No hostile humanlike faction can naturally generate the selected xenotypes, so natural tunnel raids will not occur. Select more xenotypes or use the override.
LanguageData.TunnelRaids.Message.OverrideNotCombatant: {0} cannot generate as a combatant, so it cannot be used for the override and no faction raids with it naturally. Select a different xenotype.
LanguageData.TunnelRaids.Message.OverrideDisabledMult: The override was turned off because it needs exactly one selected xenotype. Select a single xenotype to enable it again.
LanguageData.TunnelRaids.Message.FactionUnusable: {0} is selected but cannot send tunnel raids. {1}
LanguageData.TunnelRaids.Message.FactionNotInWorld: {0} is selected but no faction of that type exists in the current world, so it cannot raid here.
LanguageData.TunnelRaids.Message.XenotypeScopeNotice: The xenotype filter only decides which factions can use tunnels. Eligible factions can still send raiders of other xenotypes.
LanguageData.TunnelRaids.Message.EstimateNotice: No game is running, so natural xenotype matches are estimated from loaded definitions. A faction's ideology in a running world can change them.
